reason: Directly reviews the teneurin family structure and function, explicitly covering TENM3 (also called ODZ3/TEN3). Teneurins are the exact protein family TENM3 belongs to, and their developmental biology (synaptic specificity, cell-surface adhesion) is mechanistically relevant to TENM3-associated coloboma and microphthalmia.

The paper explicitly studies SLC4A11 as an ammonia transporter - this provides direct mechanistic insight into SLC4A11 function. While the disease context is hepatocellular carcinoma, understanding how SLC4A11 operates as a transporter is foundational to understanding its pathological role in corneal dystrophy (CHED2, FECD4). The gene is studied at the molecular level.

SEMA4A is a semaphorin and this review covers semaphorin biology in immune cell responses. SEMA4A has documented roles in both immune regulation and retinal function - the two are not mutually exclusive. With an empty abstract, caution favors inclusion; semaphorin receptor biology reviewed here is mechanistically relevant to understanding SEMA4A's diverse cellular roles.

Steroid-induced glaucoma has a well-established link to MYOC (myocilin), which is expressed in trabecular meshwork and implicated in steroid-induced intraocular pressure elevation. A clinical management review of steroid-induced glaucoma is squarely relevant to the MYOC gene library entry.

LRAT (lecithin retinol acyltransferase) esterifies retinol to retinyl esters in the visual cycle; enzymes that hydrolyze retinyl esters are the complementary arm of the same pathway. A paper on retinyl ester hydrolytic enzymes is directly relevant to LRAT's biochemical context and mutations causing Leber congenital amaurosis.

SWI/SNF complexes in cancer therapeutics. ARID2 is tracked for intellectual disability / ophthalmic genetics, not oncology. With an empty abstract and a cancer-therapy framing, this paper does not connect to the ophthalmic or neurodevelopmental rationale for including ARID2 in the library.

The abstract confirms the paper is specifically about SWI/SNF dysregulation in human lung diseases (malignant and non-malignant). ARID2 is tracked for intellectual disability and ophthalmic genetics; a lung disease focus is off-topic for this library regardless of ARID2 being a PBAF subunit.

Wagner vitreoretinal degeneration is a vitreoretinal disease directly within the scope of this gene entry (search keywords include vitreoretinopathy, stickler-syndrome). COL2A1 and VCAN/CSPG2 (also in search keywords) are both implicated in vitreoretinal conditions; a clinical paper on Wagner syndrome is relevant to the library's ophthalmic focus.

The paper studies a COL11A1 variant in relation to adult height in a Chinese population. The ophthalmic rationale for COL11A1 in this library is Stickler syndrome and vitreoretinopathy; a population genetics study of height is not relevant to the gene's ocular disease context.

The abstract explicitly describes the paper as studying ColXIa1 in myocardial morphogenesis and heart valve development. Cardiac function research is off-topic for an ophthalmic genetics library. While COL11A1 mutations underlie Stickler syndrome, cardiac development is not part of the gene's ocular disease scope.

The abstract describes this as a review of autoimmunity to cartilage collagens in rheumatoid arthritis, using collagen-induced arthritis as an animal model. While COL2A1 is a cartilage collagen, the paper's focus on joint autoimmunity and rheumatoid arthritis is off-topic for the ophthalmic genetics library that tracks COL2A1 for Stickler syndrome and vitreoretinopathy.

WDPCP (Fritz/hFrtz) is known to function at the intersection of planar cell polarity and ciliogenesis. A paper linking ciliary proteins to basal body polarization and planar cell polarity is directly relevant to understanding WDPCP's mechanism, which underlies Bardet-Biedl syndrome and other ciliopathies in this library.

WDPCP/BBS15/CPLANE5 is a bona fide ciliary protein. A proteomic analysis of mammalian primary cilia is directly relevant - it would be expected to include or inform the ciliary localization of WDPCP. With an empty abstract the confidence is moderate, but the topic matches WDPCP's core biology.

WDPCP (Fritz) functions together with INTU and FUZZY as a planar cell polarity effector complex. A paper on Intu and primary cilia in cell differentiation is directly relevant to the WDPCP/Fritz/INTU/FUZZY ciliopathy pathway. This is mechanistically central to WDPCP's role in Bardet-Biedl syndrome.

WDPCP is a WD40-repeat protein whose mutations cause Bardet-Biedl syndrome (a ciliopathy). The abstract explicitly reviews WDR proteins in ciliopathies and endocrine disorders, which is precisely the disease context for WDPCP. This review likely covers WDPCP or its closely related family members.

FZD4 and FZD5 are frizzled Wnt receptors directly tracked in this entry. A paper on how alternative Wnt signaling is initiated by distinct frizzled receptors is mechanistically central to understanding FZD4 (FEVR) and FZD5 (coloboma) function. The search keywords explicitly include both genes.

The paper directly studies eye defect etiology in a mouse model, examining extracellular matrix (glycosaminoglycans, laminin) in developing eye structures. FREM1 and CRYGB are both associated with structural eye anomalies (microphthalmia, cataract). A paper specifically about ECM disruption in the developing eye is relevant to both genes.

CHST6 encodes the sulfotransferase responsible for sulfating corneal keratan sulfate; its mutations abolish corneal keratan sulfate sulfation, causing macular corneal dystrophy. A paper specifically characterizing corneal keratan sulfate biochemistry is foundational to understanding CHST6's substrate and disease mechanism.

Although a Col4a1 mouse model is used, the paper's subject is tendon basement membrane biology and adhesion formation after tendon injury. The ophthalmic rationale for COL4A1 is anterior segment dysgenesis, cataract, and retinal disease. Tendon adhesion pathophysiology is not relevant to the ocular disease focus of this library entry.

The abstract explicitly addresses Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) - the precise disease caused by COL8A2 mutations. The paper studies oxidative stress in corneal endothelial cells in an FECD model, which is directly in-scope for a library tracking COL8A2 (FECD1, FECD). Highly relevant regardless of the specific therapeutic being tested.
